subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Uncertainty vs. Known Risk
description: A quick win: understand Uncertainty vs. Known Risk.

hook.text: Frank Knight drew a crucial line: risk is measurable, uncertainty is not. A coin flip is risk.

buildup.text: Insurance works because risk is quantifiable. Actuaries calculate car accident rates precisely over millions of drivers.

discovery.text: True uncertainty has no known probabilities. No one could calculate the odds of the internet existing before it was.

twist.text: People treat uncertainty as risk by assigning fake probabilities.

climax.text: Knowing whether you face risk or uncertainty changes the optimal strategy. Risk can be managed.

punchline.text: Risk is a known gamble. Uncertainty is fog. Confusing them is dangerous.

quiz.question: What is the difference between risk and uncertainty according to Frank Knight?
options: Risk has measurable probabilities; uncertainty does not
